critique.evidence: Desktop has a strong cyber-lab identity, confident headline, restrained cyan/red palette, and clear primary hierarchy. However, responsive polish breaks down sharply: tablet and mobile atlas columns are visibly clipped at the left edge, labels and cards begin mid-content, and the grid leaves large dead areas. The mobile card becomes excessively tall, while dense tiny monospace metadata and low-contrast secondary text weaken readability. The actual tablet/mobile header also exposes a cropped horizontal navigation rail, with mobile showing a stray partial “0”; contrast verification remains incomplete for numerous header nodes.
critique.fix: Redesign the atlas below desktop as a deliberate single-stage or horizontally scrollable carousel with visible boundaries, intact first/last cards, and a compact detail panel; remove the oversized empty grid height. Replace the clipped global nav with a compact menu or clearly signposted scroller, eliminate partial labels, raise small-text contrast and size, and tighten mobile spacing so the hierarchy remains intentional rather than desktop content cropped into a narrow viewport.
